questions.question: Analyse the effect of a cash sale of R9 000 at a mark-up of 50 percent on cost on the accounting equation.
questions.expected_answer: Cost price = 9 000 x 100 / 150 = R6 000. Assets: Bank +R9 000 and Trading stock -R6 000 (net +R3 000). Owner's equity: +R9 000 (Sales, income) and -R6 000 (Cost of sales, expense), net +R3 000. Liabilities: no effect.

questions.question: Explain why receiving R3 600 from a debtor and paying R5 000 to a creditor do not affect owner's equity.
questions.expected_answer: The receipt exchanges one asset for another: Bank +R3 600, Debtors control -R3 600; the income was recorded when the goods were sold on credit. The payment reduces an asset and a liability: Bank -R5 000, Creditors control -R5 000; settling a debt is not an expense. Neither makes the owner richer or poorer.

questions.question: Kasi Cycles started November with assets of R70 000, liabilities of R8 000 and owner's equity of R62 000, and ended with liabilities of R11 000 and owner's equity of R62 800. Calculate the final assets and the profit, and verify the profit from sales R22 500, cost of sales R15 000 and expenses R6 700.
questions.expected_answer: Assets = 62 800 + 11 000 = R73 800. Profit = increase in owner's equity = 62 800 - 62 000 = R800. Check: gross profit 22 500 - 15 000 = R7 500; net profit 7 500 - 6 700 = R800.
